heading: Cockroach spotted on cardiologist Ashok Seth’s dinner table at Mumbai JW Marriott; he tags Tukaram Mundhe and FSSAI; is food hygiene really such a big ask?
author: TOI Lifestyle Desk / etimes.in /  Sep 21, 2026, 19:21 IST
paragraphs: A dinner at a luxury hotel in Mumbai took an unexpected turn after Padma Bhushan AND cardiologist Dr Ashok Seth said he spotted a baby cockroach crawling on his table
Seth was dining at the Romano restaurant at JW Marriott, Sahar, Mumbai, on Saturday evening when he noticed the cockroach moving around the dishes

Later, on Sunday he posted a video of the incident on X and tagged Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) and JW Marriott.“Roachie came for dinner”Seth described the unexpected guest in a sarcastic post on X. "Look who came for dinner unexpectedly. 'Roachie' - a baby cockroach was on our table wanting to share our dinner at the Romano restaurant at JW Marriott, Sahar, Mumbai, Saturday night!!!" he wrote
He said attempts to make the cockroach leave did not work. "Despite our persuasion, 'Roachie' refused to leave
The incident affected his appetite, and he said he and his companions eventually left the restaurant without finishing their dinner. "But he (the cockroach) really took our appetite away

We left," he wrote.He tagged Tukaram Mundhe in the postSeth also tagged Maharashtra FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe in his post. "Thankfully we are in Mr Mundhe's territory and he most likely will look into this also," he wrote

Mundhe has been involved in food-safety inspections and enforcement action in Maharashtra since taking charge as FDA commissioner in May 2026.“This is a five-star hotel”Speaking to NDTV on Monday, Seth said he viewed the incident as a hygiene concern rather than simply an unpleasant experience during dinner. "We spotted one cockroach on the table, I am sure there will be more in the kitchen
This shows the restaurant’s extremely casual attitude towards hygiene," he told NDTV
Seth also said he had been dining with foreign delegates and described the incident as "an embarrassment for the country." "This is a five-star hotel

They must do better," he said.Reaction from the netizensThe incident has since drawn attention online because of Seth's unusual description of the cockroach as "Roachie" and his reference to pizza and pasta in the social media post.One user wrote, "80 years on since independence, we are yet to learn the significance of health and hygiene, civic sense, cleanliness, sincerity, dedication and moral values! Sick! For now, we need Tukaram Mundhes in every city ... but sadly, corruption rules the roost!" Another user wrote, "If you have the visitor on your table, I can only dread what party is going on in the kitchen." A third user wrote, "Yes
In all hotels, kitchen hygiene is of very low standards
The workers in the kitchen also lack hygiene and do not follow proper hand-washing techniques

It all starts in the kitchen, and it is one area that should be audited by hotel managers regularly."Is expecting hygienic food really too much to ask?The incident comes at a time when food-safety checks in Mumbai have already brought several establishments under scrutiny

In June 2026, the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspended the licences of six food establishments after inspections found violations including poor hygiene, cockroach infestations, foul odour, leaking refrigerators and expired food products
Among the establishments named were Flint & Waarsa at the NCPA in Nariman Point, M.K
Bakery in Borivali East and Hotel Shree Krishna in Bhandup West.For customers paying premium prices at high-end hotels and restaurants, the expectation is not that high
It is just that the food they are served should meet essential hygiene and safety standards

The question, therefore, is very simple: when customers are paying more for a meal, is expecting hygienic food really too much to ask?Looking for trusted parenting advice?
